statement: For every relative-error model and every finite nonempty binary tree of real pairs, if (depth+1)*u < 1, the rounded sum along the tree of its rounded leaf products equals the exact sum of a same-shaped tree of perturbed exact products. Each product x is changed to y with |y-x| <= gamma(depth+1,u)*|x|, where gamma(k,u) = k*u/(1-k*u). The perturbations apply to products, without a claim of separate perturbations to their factors.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: A model m consists of a real u >= 0 and a function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z*(1+delta). T is any finite nonempty ordered binary tree with leaf labels (a,b) in R x R. Its depth is d(leaf(a,b)) = 0 and d(node(L,R)) = 1 + max(d(L),d(R)). No balance, equal leaf depth, or restrictions on the real leaf values are assumed. For every such m and T, let k = d(T)+1 in the natural numbers, cast to a real in real arithmetic. If k*u < 1, then there exists a real-labelled tree P such that IsPerturbation(gamma(k,u), exactProductTree(T), P) and exactSum(P) = roundedDotProduct(m,T). Here gamma(k,u) = k*u/(1-k*u). The relation IsPerturbation(B,X,P) is generated by the leaf rule |y-x| <= B*|x| for corresponding leaf labels x,y and by applying the relation to both respective children of a node. Thus P has exactly the same ordered shape as T, and for each leaf occurrence i of T labelled (a_i,b_i), its corresponding real label y_i in P satisfies |y_i-a_i*b_i| <= gamma(k,u)*|a_i*b_i|. exactSum returns the leaf label at a leaf and the ordinary real sum of the two child results at a node. Consequently the exact sum of these y_i equals the rounded reduction of the rounded leaf products using the grouping of T, as defined by roundedDotProduct. The existential witness perturbs the products, without asserting perturbations of the two factors separately or specifying an algorithm for selecting P.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R) mapping each leaf (a,b) to the ordinary real product a*b while retaining every node and its left/right order. Explicitly E(leaf(a,b)) = leaf(a*b) and E(node(L,R)) = node(E(L),E(R)). It performs no summation or balancing. This is the reference tree whose leaf values the target theorem perturbs.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: For every model m with rounding function r and every T in Tree(R x R), replace each leaf (a,b) by r(a*b), preserving ordered shape. Explicitly Q_m(leaf(a,b)) = leaf(r(a*b)) and Q_m(node(L,R)) = node(Q_m(L),Q_m(R)). Model.mul(m,a,b) is defined as r(a*b). This performs one rounded multiplication per leaf and no additions; its output is passed to roundedSum by roundedDotProduct.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: For every model m and T in Tree(R x R), this real-valued function is roundedSum(m,roundedProductTree(m,T)). For a real-labelled tree, roundedSum(m,leaf(v)) = v and roundedSum(m,node(L,R)) = r(roundedSum(m,L)+roundedSum(m,R)), because Model.add(m,x,y) = r(x+y). Equivalently D_m(leaf(a,b)) = r(a*b) and D_m(node(L,R)) = r(D_m(L)+D_m(R)). It rounds each leaf product and then each internal addition according to the existing tree grouping; it does not choose a tree, balance it, or round a leaf again during summation. On a path with h internal nodes there are h addition roundings after the product rounding, at most d(T)+1 roundings in total. These constructions are defined for every model and tree; the inequality (d(T)+1)*u < 1 is needed only as a hypothesis of the target theorem, which represents this returned value as the exact sum of a same-shaped perturbation of exactProductTree(T).

assumptions: A model m consists of a real u >= 0 and a function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z*(1+delta).

T is any finite nonempty ordered binary tree with leaf labels (a,b) in R x R. Its depth is d(leaf(a,b)) = 0 and d(node(L,R)) = 1 + max(d(L),d(R)). No balance, equal leaf depth, or restrictions on the real leaf values are assumed.
The theorem additionally requires (d(T)+1)*u < 1. Natural depths and d(T)+1 are cast to reals where multiplied by u; this hypothesis gives a positive denominator in gamma.
IsPerturbation uses the same bound at every corresponding leaf and preserves ordered tree shape. An exact zero leaf product must remain zero. No individual-factor perturbation is required.
The rounding property holds for all real inputs. No representable set, particular floating-point format, rounding mode, or other rounding property is supplied or assumed.
